title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 82
paragraphs: After his return, his political enemies brought him up before the Ephors, alleging that he had accepted bribes and so had failed to take Argos when he could easily have done so. He answered them — whether lying or telling the truth I cannot say for certain — that once he had captured the sanctuary of Argos, it seemed to him that the god's oracle had been fulfilled, and therefore he did not think it right to attempt the city itself until he had consulted the omens and learned whether the goddess would allow him or stand against him. As he was taking the auspices in the temple of Hera, a flame of fire blazed out from the breasts of the cult statue, and by this he knew the truth of the matter: that he would not take Argos. Had the flame blazed from the head of the image, he would have conquered the city entire from top to bottom; but since it came from the breasts, everything the god had wanted him to accomplish had already been done. So he spoke, and the Spartans found his account credible and reasonable, and he easily escaped his accusers.
